transcript.text: Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. To address this, pharmacy can remove bedside stock and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.

transcript.text: I want to flag a laboratory medicine issue for the safety review. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. We need to make sure nursing and the clinical teams are aware that aPTT, not anti-Xa, will be used for monitoring until Friday evening.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From a nursing education standpoint, I need to flag a staffing competency issue. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not yet completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Under our current policy, each of those nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they can administer this medication. This is something we need to account for in the safeguards before the protocol goes live on the night shift.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on bedside stock of the intravenous anticoagulant; pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes only, with layered safeguards including electronic ordering alert, aPTT monitoring, and charge-nurse sign-off for untrained nurses, effective for the night shift pending full medication safety review completion.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Remove bedside stock from automated dispensing cabinets; supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold to eliminate concentration selection errors at the point of dispensing.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Use aPTT testing every six hours as the approved monitoring method until the anti-Xa analyzer is calibrated and available on Friday at 17:00. Clear communication to nursing and clinical teams is required before the night shift begins.
decisions.nurse_authorization: All 18 nurses on tonight's shift who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module must receive charge-nurse sign-off before administering this medication, per current policy. Charge nurses must be notified of this requirement before the shift begins.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority concentration-selection alert in the electronic medication record at 16:00 today, requiring clinician acknowledgment before the order can be released. This must be confirmed active before the night shift begins.

commitments.detail: Remove bedside stock of the anticoagulant from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold.
Communicate aPTT every-six-hours monitoring requirement to nursing and clinical teams before the night shift; transition to anti-Xa monitoring after calibration on Friday at 17:00.
Notify charge nurses of their sign-off responsibility for the 18 nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module before tonight's shift begins.
Deploy the concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today and confirm it is active before the night shift begins.
Issue a unified safety directive summarizing all layered safeguards to nursing, pharmacy, laboratory, and clinical teams before the night shift begins.
